q: 1. Specified compressive strength of concrete is obtained from cube tests at the end of
explain: By convention and IS code practice, the characteristic/specified compressive strength of concrete is defined based on 28-day cube test results, by which time hydration has developed most of the strength.

q: 2. The strength of concrete after one year as compared to 28 days strength is about
explain: Continued hydration over time increases strength beyond the 28-day value; typical long-term gain at one year is about 20-25% more than the 28-day strength.

q: 3. The ratio of various ingredients in concrete of grade M20 is
explain: M20 grade concrete corresponds to the nominal mix proportion of 1:1.5:3 (cement:fine aggregate:coarse aggregate) as per traditional nominal mix classification.

q: 4. In concrete mix design, allowance for bulking of sand is necessary in case of
explain: Bulking changes the apparent volume of sand due to moisture, so a correction is required only when proportioning is done by volume (volume batching), not by weight.

q: 5. In concrete mix design, allowance for surface water carried by aggregate is necessary in case of
explain: Surface moisture on aggregate adds extra water to the mix and affects the effective water-cement ratio regardless of whether batching is done by volume or by weight, so an allowance is needed in both cases.

q: 6. According to I.S. : 456, the number of grades of concrete mixes, is
explain: As per IS:456, concrete mixes were historically classified into 7 grades based on specified compressive strengths (though modern codes list more, this classic reference lists 7).

q: 7. The preliminary test is repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimens, exceeds
explain: If the compressive strength results of three specimens from a preliminary test vary by more than 15 kg/cm², the test is considered unreliable and must be repeated.

q: 8. The approximate ratio of direct tensile strength to direct compressive strength test of concrete
explain: Concrete is inherently weak in tension compared to compression; its direct tensile strength is only about 1/10th (approximately 0.10) of its direct compressive strength.

q: 9. The concrete in which preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
explain: Controlled concrete is that for which preliminary trial mixes and tests are conducted to design and control the exact proportions for target strength.

q: 10. The workability of concrete by slump test is expressed as
explain: The result of a slump test is simply the vertical subsidence of the concrete cone, measured and expressed in millimetres (mm).

q: 11. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
explain: The allowable (permissible) shear strength value used in design is directly based on the concrete's own inherent shear strength characteristics.

q: 12. Minimum number of test specimens required for finding the compressive strength of concrete are
explain: As per standard practice, a minimum of 3 test specimens (cubes) are cast and tested to determine the compressive strength of a concrete batch.

q: 13. For the construction of the retaining structures, the type of concrete mix to be used, is
explain: For retaining structures which require higher strength due to lateral earth pressures, a richer mix of 1:1½:3 (M20 grade) is typically used.

q: 14. The correct proportion of ingredients of concrete, depends upon
explain: Correct mix proportioning must account for all these factors - bulking of sand, water content, absorption of aggregates, and desired workability - to achieve an accurate and effective concrete mix.

q: 15. The concrete shrinkage is more pronounced in
explain: A rich mix contains a higher proportion of cement paste (which is the shrinking component), so shrinkage is more pronounced in rich mixes compared to lean mixes.

q: 16. For finding compressive strength of concrete, the minimum number of cubes required is
explain: As per standard testing practice, a minimum of 3 concrete cubes are cast and tested to determine the average compressive strength for a given sample.

q: 17. The 28 days cube strength of mass concrete using aggregates of maximum size 5 cm for gravity dams should be
explain: For mass concrete in gravity dams using large aggregate (5 cm max size), the required 28-day cube strength is relatively modest, typically specified as below 200 kg/cm², since strength requirements are lower than structural concrete.

q: 18. The behavior of concrete under instantaneous loads is
explain: Under instantaneous (short-duration) loading, concrete behaves approximately as an elastic material, following a near-linear stress-strain relationship.

q: 19. Concrete can take tension up to
options: 10% of the compressive strength of steel
10% of the combined compressive strength of concrete & R/F
10% of the total tensile strength of the section
explain: Concrete's tensile strength is generally only about 10% of its own compressive strength, reflecting its characteristic weakness in tension relative to compression.

q: 20. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement cube after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the minimum 7-day compressive strength requirement for OPC mortar cubes is 17.5 N/mm².

q: 21. For cylindrical specimens, the dimension of cylinder generally used
explain: The standard cylindrical test specimen used for compressive strength testing has a diameter of 15 cm and a height of 30 cm, giving the standard height-to-diameter ratio of 2.

q: 22. The test conducted in the labouratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is carried out in the laboratory on specimens made from trial concrete mixes to establish suitable proportions before actual construction begins.

q: 23. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
explain: The allowable shear strength of concrete is generally derived as a function of, and depends upon, its compressive strength, as per design code provisions.

q: 24. Permissible compressive strength of M150 concrete grade is
explain: As indicated by its designation, the M150 grade of concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 150 kg/cm².

q: 25. Permissible compressive strength of M200 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M200 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 200 kg/cm².

q: 26. Permissible compressive strength of M250 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M250 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 250 kg/cm².

q: 27. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is a laboratory test performed on trial mix specimens to determine and finalize the mix design before actual site work begins.

q: 28. The preliminary test should be repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimen exceeds.
explain: As per the acceptance criteria in this text, if the compressive strength results of the three test specimens vary by more than 1.5 N/mm², the preliminary test must be repeated.

q: 29. The factors which affects the design of concrete mix is
explain: Concrete mix design is influenced jointly by aggregate fineness modulus, water-cement ratio, and required workability (slump) — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 30. M150 grade of concrete approximates
explain: The M150 grade of concrete approximately corresponds to a nominal mix ratio of 1:2:4 (cement:sand:aggregate).

q: 31. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Well-graded aggregate reduces void content and improves the flow characteristics of the mix, thereby directly improving workability.

q: 32. The compressive strength of 100 mm cube as compared to 150 mm cube is always
explain: Due to the size effect in concrete testing, smaller 100 mm cube specimens generally record a higher apparent compressive strength than standard 150 mm cubes.

q: 33. According to IS 456, the number of grades of concrete mix is
explain: As per the classification referenced in this text (older IS 456 provisions), concrete mixes are designated into seven standard grades.

q: 34. For the construction of the retaining structures, the type of concrete mix to be used is
explain: For retaining structures, a richer mix of proportion 1:1.5:3 (equivalent to M20 grade) is recommended for adequate strength and durability.

q: 35. If the average compressive strength is 4000 kg/cm2 and standard deviation is 500, the coefficient of variation is
explain: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (500/4000) x 100 = 12.5%.

q: 36. Gel space ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: volume of hydrated cement to the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores
the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores to volume of hydrated cement
both a) and b) of above
explain: Gel-space ratio is defined by Powers as the volume of the gel (hydration products) divided by the sum of the volume of the gel and the capillary pore space it occupies.

q: 37. For batching 1:3:6 concrete mix by volume, the ingredients required per bag of 50 kg cement are
options: 70 litres of sand and 120 litres of aggregates
70 kg of sand and 140 litres of aggregates
105 litres of sand and 140 litres of aggregates
105 litres of sand and 210 litres of aggregates
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix, with one bag of cement corresponding to about 35 litres, the sand requirement (3×35=105 litres) and coarse aggregate requirement (6×35=210 litres) work out to 105 litres of sand and 210 litres of aggregate.

q: 38. The dimensions of 35 litres forma for measuring aggregates by volume are
options: length 30 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 30 cm
length 39 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 32 cm
length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, height 48 cm
length 22 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 40 cm
explain: As per the standard farma box dimensions given in this text, a box measuring 22 cm × 25 cm × 40 cm gives a volume corresponding to 35 litres.

q: 39. Light weight concrete is used in
explain: Because of its lower strength and density, light weight concrete finds its principal application in non-load-bearing wall construction such as partition walls.

q: 40. For mass concrete in piers and abutments, the concrete mix used is of proportion.
explain: For mass concrete work such as piers and abutments, a leaner mix of proportion 1:3:6 is generally used, as high strength is not the primary requirement.

q: 41. The correct proportioning of various ingredients of concrete largely depend upon.............
explain: Correct mix proportioning must account for bulking of sand, water content, and aggregate absorption together — all of these factors affect the actual quantities batched.

q: 42. The concrete in which preliminary tests are preformed for designing the mix is called:
explain: Controlled concrete refers to concrete whose mix proportions are determined and controlled through preliminary laboratory tests to meet specified strength and durability requirements.
